register.name: Water Sector Modernization Program
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Loan 9490-DO · Approved 24 March 2023 · closing date 31 December 2027
register.note: US$60.68 million disbursed at the third restructuring, June 2026
register.text: An IBRD loan of US$250 million, a US$225 million Program-for-Results and a US$25 million investment project financing, to improve the planning and efficiency of selected water institutions and to increase access to safely managed water and sanitation services in selected water-stressed areas. US$60.68 million had been disbursed by its third restructuring, in June 2026; it serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Support to the National Housing Program
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Loan 9392-DO · loan agreement of 26 July 2022 · closing date extended to 30 June 2027
register.note: Amount not stated in the letter opened; implementation to move to the Ministry of Housing, Habitat and Buildings
register.text: An IBRD loan to the Dominican Republic in support of its National Housing Program, under a loan agreement of 26 July 2022. In a letter of 16 October 2025 the World Bank extended its closing date to 30 June 2027 and agreed, subject to conditions, to amend the agreement so that the Ministry of Housing, Habitat and Buildings (MIVHED) implements it. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Sustainable finance and trade package for Banco BHD
register.detail: IFC · 13 August 2026 · two subordinated loans of up to $75M and $50M · GTFP trade line of up to $30M
register.note: Up to $155 million in all; the subordinated loans include capital mobilised from other commercial investors
register.text: An IFC package of up to US$155 million for Banco BHD: two subordinated loans, with capital mobilised from other commercial investors, and a trade line under the Global Trade Finance Program. The long-term finance goes to distributed solar energy, renewable generation and storage, sustainable construction and blue finance, and the trade line supports firms, including small and medium-sized enterprises, that import and export; it serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Financing for small businesses and climate, Banco Promerica RD
register.detail: IDB Invest · 15 January 2026 · $20M senior loan · $5M subordinated loan · $10M blended loan from the Finland-LAC Blended Finance Climate Fund
register.note: A package of up to $80 million, including $45 million mobilised from FMO, the Eco.business Fund and Enabling Qapital
register.text: A financing package of up to US$80 million approved by IDB Invest for Banco Múltiple Promerica de la República Dominicana, to expand credit to small and medium-sized enterprises and to finance sustainability projects. The blended loan carries performance-based incentives tied to the growth of the bank’s green portfolio; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Long-term financing for small businesses, Banco Caribe
register.detail: IDB Invest · 10 June 2025 · senior loan of up to $25M · tenor of up to five years · We-Fi incentives of up to $150,000
register.note: With performance-based incentives to grow lending to women-owned or led small and medium-sized enterprises
register.text: Up to US$25 million in long-term financing from IDB Invest to Banco Múltiple Caribe Internacional, to increase access to capital for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the Dominican Republic. A blended component of up to US$150,000 from We-Fi rewards growth in the bank’s portfolio of women-owned or led businesses; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Subordinated loan for women-led businesses, Banco BHD
register.detail: IDB Invest · 8 January 2024 · $75M subordinated loan · tenor of up to seven years
register.note: Loans in Dominican pesos to micro, small and medium-sized businesses led or owned by women
register.text: A US$75 million subordinated loan from IDB Invest to Banco BHD, with a tenor of up to seven years, to increase access to credit through loans in Dominican pesos for micro, small and medium-sized businesses led or owned by women. It serves the livelihood standard.

enterprises.heading: Already working in the Dominican Republic.

items.name: DREAM Project
items.text: A non-profit on the north coast, founded in 1995, that provides educational opportunities to children, youth and families, from early childhood education and literacy to youth leadership, and in 2023 served more than 7,000 children and youth a year. It was one of six winners of the UNESCO International Literacy Prizes in 2023, and in 2025 took its My Very Own Library reading programme to rural public schools.

items.name: Instituto 512
items.text: An institute for school leadership and teacher training that, with Mentu, has launched Lucero, a platform of six tools based on artificial intelligence (four for teachers, two for management teams) to plan lessons, guide teaching strategies and involve families in learning. It is piloted in 25 schools of the Modelo FARO in the 2025–2026 school year, for an estimated 189 teachers and more than 4,500 students.

items.name: Perfecto Labs
items.text: A non-profit headquartered in Yamasá, a rural town, that runs the Perfectico AI Incubator, where young people aged 10 to 18 in underserved communities learn artificial intelligence and programming by building low-cost answers to problems they face, such as a cacao bean sorting machine. It was a semi-finalist in MIT Solve’s 2025 Global Learning Challenge.

items.name: Hábitat para la Humanidad República Dominicana
items.text: The Dominican affiliate of Habitat for Humanity, which replaces dirt floors with concrete (2,476 by fiscal year 2024) and connects homes to sewers; its housing microfinance programme has mobilised US$25.6 million and reached more than 8,000 families renovating their homes. With IDB Lab it has signed an agreement to bring pay-for-results financing to sanitation in the Dominican Republic.

items.name: Banco Adopem
items.text: A savings and credit bank, operating since 2004, that grew out of ADOPEM, an association founded in 1982 to give microcredit to Dominican women ready to start a business. In an IDB Invest analysis of more than 170,000 of its loans, 89% of its women clients were considered economically vulnerable, and women held 67% of the active loans in its small-business portfolio.
